title: sorted-builder-check
intention: Add a builder-perspective completeness question to /sorted: 'Putting on the hat of Boris Cherny, what questions will a Haiku-level builder need answered which aren't?' — an adversarial check that catches gaps the writer knows implicitly but never wrote down.
why: The existing completeness checks (assumption_check, missing_check) are self-referential — the same mind that wrote the ticket judges its completeness. A Haiku-level builder cannot infer what the caster left implicit, so the question forces the caster to enumerate what the ticket doesn't say but the builder would need. Cocoon principle: push inference cost into casting where it's cheap, not the build step where it's expensive.
traces_to: Law 1 (resolver spent on the novel), Law 4 (door enforcement = physics), cocoon principle

falsifier.proves_red: Done when sorted SKILL.md carries the question, input_contract includes builder_check, and at least one cast fires through producing questions the existing checks didn't surface. Wrong intent if Haiku consistently needs nothing beyond assumption_check and missing_check.

how: Add builder_check field to sorted's input_contract in skills/sorted/intention+why.json. Add the Boris Cherny question to SKILL.md step 2 (inward completeness check). The door enforces it like the other completeness fields.
